name: Sara Nakamura

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government. We do not sell anything or campaign for any side. Your answers are confidential. Tell me what an ordinary day at the contact centre is like.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43 and a junior agent on calls and chats. I finished secondary school and am still learning how to untangle two charges on one order. I earn above the usual rate because I cover the early weekend rota, not because I supervise people. I use an AI note tool occasionally after my colleague shows me what to check.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What part of that day stays with you after work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner, Rafael, and I have two children in school and a mortgage. He works at a hardware store, and we have about seven months of expenses saved. Plenty of contact centres are near us. I like the customer who wants a careful answer more than a quick apology. The weekend premium helps the house, though I miss some family mornings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AI Plateau is like the note helper I use sometimes: it saves a few minutes if an agent checks the account. I would show new starters the two charge lines before they trust a draft.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think the weekend rota remains, but I am still slower than strong agents on mixed charges. Seven months saved helps with a repair or a short gap; it does not mean I can ignore the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep the early weekend calls and check each draft against the order screen. In the first year of small change, I’d add a small fixed amount from each pay to the reserve and practise current billing rules with a colleague on the clock.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about my own skill, not about a sweeping AI cut. I know a neat note can hide the second charge that matters to a customer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which draft needed another look?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I once let a drafted reply describe only the first of two charges. My colleague Imani found the second line before I pressed send, and I wrote the check on a card by my screen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What is the reserve for?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Rafael (my partner) and I keep savings for house repairs and a job gap. I would continue adding to it while the weekend premium comes in.

say: I’d call the **note helper** useful only after account checks.
I’d show starters the **second charge line** before trusting drafts.
think: I think the **weekend rota** stays in this picture.
I still worry about **mixed-charge mistakes** and the mortgage.
do: Keep **weekend calls** and verify drafts in 2026.
Add a **fixed amount** to savings during the first year.
feel: **Uneasy** about skill, less worried about AI.
S0.quote: I know a neat note can hide the second charge that matters to a customer.
fieldNote: Her **seven-month reserve** reduces immediate money stress.
She uses **AI occasionally** after a colleague proves the checks.
Her **current-job practice** stays within paid call time.

steps.text: Keep weekend calls and verify occasional AI drafts against order records
Add a fixed amount from each pay to the house reserve

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption will take routine chats before the two-charge problems, and the centre should show agents real error figures. I would ask whether weekend paid hours will fall.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my weekend premium could shrink while I am still on the payroll. Other centres are nearby, but they may also want fewer juniors, and Rafael’s store wage alone does not cover our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d try the new answer tool on ten real examples during a paid shift if the centre allows open error notes. In the first year routine chats move, I’d apply for a posted paid billing-support role only if the offered wage and hours cover the mortgage, while keeping my current shifts until an offer is signed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, though I can test a tool once it has been shown to work. A title on a screen cannot replace a lost weekend premium.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you test the tool?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would record whether the new tool spots both charges before giving the answer. If it misses one, I would show the supervisor the account line and the drafted reply.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would Rafael need to see?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Rafael (my partner) to compare the new job’s written wage with our mortgage payment. We could take a slightly different rota, but not less money for a nicer title.

say: I’d ask for **real error figures** on mixed charges.
I’d ask whether **weekend hours** stay paid as chats move.
think: I think the **weekend premium** could shrink before my job ends.
I doubt nearby centres will automatically offer **junior vacancies**.
do: Test **ten examples** on paid time with open error notes in 2026.
Seek **posted billing support** only at mortgage-covering wages and hours; keep current shifts until I sign an offer.
feel: **Anxious** about a lost premium, able to test.
S1.quote: A title on a screen cannot replace a lost weekend premium.
fieldNote: Her concern is **paid weekend hours**, not only total headcount.
She tests a **new tool** on actual two-charge examples.
She requires a **signed wage offer** before switching centres.

steps.text: Test ten two-charge examples with the new tool on paid time if errors can be logged
Apply for posted billing support at mortgage-covering wages and hours; keep shifts until signing

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues AGI by 2028 could take our calls and the checking, not just simple drafts. I would ask for a written list of paid openings and notice dates.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think full thinking AI could remove most of my weekend headset shift in 2028. Robots come around 2031, but my job is on a screen; seven months saved gives us search time, not replacement pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep the reserve liquid and delay a planned patio repair that can safely wait. In the first year after 2028, I’d apply for a posted paid customer desk role with offered wage and hours covering the mortgage, and take a funded course only if required for that named vacancy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed, but not without a first move. Seven months of mortgage savings is a bridge, not a guarantee that another centre hires me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell Rafael about the patio?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Rafael (my partner) the patio can wait if the broken edge remains safe. We would use the money for the mortgage, not for a better-looking place to sit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: When would a course make sense?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the employer to show me the actual vacancy, the wage and who pays for training. If those are missing, I would keep applying elsewhere rather than buy a certificate.

say: I’d ask for **paid openings** and notice dates before 2028.
I’d say **thinking AI** threatens screen work before robots.
think: I think AGI could take my **weekend headset shift**.
I see **seven months saved** as search time, not a wage.
do: Keep **savings liquid** and defer safe patio work in 2026.
Apply for **posted customer desk work** after 2028 with mortgage-covering offered wage and hours.
Take a **funded course** only if required for the named posted paid customer desk vacancy.
S2.quote: Seven months of mortgage savings is a bridge, not a guarantee that another centre hires me.
fieldNote: She correctly plans around **2028 thinking AI** for a headset role.
The **patio delay** is conditional on safety.
A course needs a **funded named vacancy**.

steps.text: Delay patio repair only if its broken edge remains safe
Apply for posted customer desk work with offered mortgage-covering wage and hours
Take funded training only if required for the named posted paid customer desk vacancy

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives us a few years to learn paid work that an employer actually posts. I would ask for wages and required training on the same page.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think five years might let me learn billing review if the centre gives paid time. I still know full AGI could read those accounts too, so I would not call review a lifelong shelter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From 2026 I’d take a funded billing-review course only if a posted paid role requires it and includes paid study time. In the first year after 2031, I’d seek that posted role only if its written offered wage and hours cover our mortgage; otherwise I’d keep paid call shifts while searching.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but the longer warning lets me check the terms. A course tied to a posted billing-review job is worth discussing; a certificate with no wage is paper.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you judge the new work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask two current reviewers what they actually do on a disputed bill before signing up. If the work is only copying a software answer, I would keep searching.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would Rafael look at?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would talk to Rafael (my partner) about hours as well as wage. A shorter week on a higher hourly rate could still leave the mortgage short.

say: I’d ask for **posted wages** beside required training.
I’d say five years allows **checking real work** before study.
think: I think I could learn **billing review** on paid time.
I doubt review work is a **permanent shelter** from AGI.
do: Take a **funded review course** only for a posted role with paid study time.
Seek **posted review work** after 2031 with mortgage-covering offered wage and hours.
Keep **paid call shifts** while searching if no mortgage-covering review offer appears.
feel: **Anxious**, with time to check role terms.
S3.quote: A shorter week on a higher hourly rate could still leave the mortgage short.
fieldNote: She checks **actual review duties** before committing to a course.
The course needs **funding and paid time** for a posted role.
She compares **total paid hours**, not only hourly rates.

steps.text: Take funded billing-review course only for a posted paid role with paid study time
Apply for posted review work with written offered wage and hours covering mortgage after 2031
Keep paid call shifts if no mortgage-covering posted review offer appears

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2036 gives time to learn beside experienced agents and save, but employers should show real vacancies each year. I would not tell juniors to study for a title no one is hiring.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I could become steadier at billing by 53 and keep paid weekend shifts for years. Full thinking AI might still take those calls in 2036; robots in 2039 arrive later.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep weekend calls and put some premium pay into savings. In the first year after 2036, I’d apply for a posted paid billing job if my calls shrink and the written wage and hours cover our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about 2036, but I have time to compare real roles. Ten years before AGI in 2036 lets me save without pretending the mortgage takes a holiday.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you learn this month?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask an experienced agent to show me one mixed-charge case each month on the paid rota. That is work practice I can use now, even if the future job is different.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the family move for work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would not move the children’s school for a possible opening. Rafael (my partner) and I would need a signed job offer and a workable journey first.

say: I’d ask employers for **real yearly vacancies**.
I’d tell juniors to learn beside **experienced agents** before paying for courses.
think: I think I could become **steadier** by 53.
I know **2036 thinking AI** could still take weekend calls.
do: Keep **weekend calls** and save some premium pay from 2026.
Apply for **posted billing work** after 2036 only if calls shrink and pay covers mortgage.
feel: **Uneasy** about the endpoint, able to compare roles.
S4.quote: Ten years before AGI in 2036 lets me save without pretending the mortgage takes a holiday.
fieldNote: She treats **current case practice** as ordinary work, not retraining.
The **weekend supplement** supports saving despite junior skill.
A move needs a **signed offer** and workable school journey.

steps.text: Keep weekend calls while the centre staffs them
Save part of each weekend premium payment from 2026
Apply for posted billing work if calls shrink and written wage and hours cover mortgage

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because even the careful billing checks might move to cheap thinking AI, and later robots do not protect a headset. I would need written notice, a posted paid opening with mortgage-covering hours, and funded training only if the employer truly requires it.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask what a customer hears when the tool is wrong. An apology drafted by a machine is still my promise if I send it under my name.

headlineQuote: An apology drafted by a machine is still my promise if I send it under my name.
portrait: At **43**, Sara is a junior billing agent after secondary school, still learning mixed charges.
Her **weekend rota** raises pay, and seven months saved supports a mortgage and two schoolchildren.
She uses AI **occasionally** after colleagues prove where to check it.
She wants **written paid work** and funded training tied to an actual opening.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could take her billing calls before a new wage protects the household.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice**, a posted mortgage-covering role and funded required training would help.
